newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco Cos win access to medicaid patients.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco Cos win access to medicaid patients.

text.p: Tobacco companies battling a Florida state lawsuit on Friday won access to the names of 400,000 Florida Medicaid patients and can closely question 25 patients for possible fraudulent or misdiagnosed treatment for smoking illlnesses.

The Philip Morris Companies and other cigarette makers argued in a pre-trial hearing that they need the names of the patients to challenge the financial claims of the state of Florida, which is suing tobacco companies for $1 billion or more in healthcare costs associated with smoking related sickness.

Palm Beach County Circuit Court Judge Harold Cohen ordered the state government to deliver the names to the tobacco companies' lawyers within 10 days. He also ordered that the names be kept secret by all parties and that the medical records of the 25 patients to be questioned be made available to the the tobacco companies' lawyers.
"This court is not going to permit the deposing of 400,000 Medicaid recipients," Cohen said.
The order, Cohen said, is to allow the tobacco companies "to pick 25 names. It's not to go out and hound 400,000 recipients."
Cohen earlier denied tobacco industry's request that the start of the Florida Medicaid lawsuit be delayed.
He has scheduled an August 4 trial in the lawsuit, one of 22 similar civil actions brought by U.S. states against cigarette makers.
